reason: The agent adds a by-name my_var_sp_row_field_by_name for ROW TYPE OF table/cursor (matching the human approach) and the ROW TYPE OF cases in main.select_into_row pass, but it leaves the pre-existing DBUG_ASSERT(0) in Type_handler_row::make_outvar_field on the explicit-ROW non-existing-field path, so 'SELECT a,b INTO r0.a,r0.b1_non_existing' with DECLARE r0 ROW(...) aborts the debug server instead of returning ER_ROW_VARIABLE_DOES_NOT_HAVE_FIELD. The issue text only mentions ROW TYPE OF, but the agent edited that very function and left an assertion-crash on an adjacent user-reachable path, which a maintainer would reject as an incomplete fix. (Its flip of check_assignability to '!= 1' is actually a correct fix of a latent bug and is not the cause of failure.)

The agent converts JSON numbers for BIT columns through a double (my_ci_strntod then Field_bit::store(double)), which loses precision and sign/overflow handling: json_table.result expects 18446744073709551615 for BIT(64) but the agent yields 9223372036854775808, 0.5/1.5 truncate to 0/1 instead of rounding to 1/2, and -1 wraps to 18446744073709551615 with no 'Out of range' warning. The issue's own [0,1] example is fixed, but a BIT(64) conversion that silently loses values is a genuine defect independent of the tests' exact expectations.

The agent does not fix the ambiguous frm parsing; it refuses CREATE VIEW with ER_WRONG_VALUE whenever the definer user/host contains a newline, so in main.view_grant 'create view v as select f()' fails instead of succeeding and later yielding ER_VIEW_INVALID on SELECT. This blocks a legitimately created user from creating any view and leaves already-written frm files unaffected, whereas the issue title asks for the frm parsing itself to be made unambiguous (human switches definer_user/host to FILE_OPTIONS_ESTRING); a maintainer would reject the workaround.

The issue title and body ask that numeric aggregates (sum, like geometry) error on XMLTYPE; the agent overrides Item_sum_sum/avg/variance_fix_length_and_dec exactly as the human does, so sum/avg/variance would raise ER_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER_DATA_TYPE_FOR_OPERATION. The test fails first on 'SELECT round(x)' and also expects floor, abs, unary minus and CAST AS signed/unsigned/float/double/decimal/time/date/datetime to error, a broader scope the developers chose but the issue does not state.

main.func_json (the issue's exact scenario) passes with the agent patch: ['ab','cd'] plus the 'Row 3 was cut' warning. main.type_json fails only on --enable_metadata output: the human additionally bumps Item_func_json_arrayagg::max_length by 2*mbminlen in fix_fields (9437184 -> 9437190), so the expected 'Length' column changed; the issue says nothing about result metadata length. No defect found in the agent's cut_max_length rewrite (the base cut is side-effect free so the double call is safe).

The agent calls sp_revoke_privileges(..., &sp_handler_package_body) a second time inside drop_routine right after the first sp_revoke_privileges, while the first call's grant-table lock is still held; Grant_tables::open_and_lock then hits the assertion 'thd->lock == 0' in lock_tables and the server aborts on 'DROP PACKAGE pkg2' in compat/oracle.sp-package-security. The human revokes both handlers inside the single locked section of sp_revoke_privileges. A crash caused by the agent change is W.
